Defaults to the folder that contains the .venv

One-time setup in Termux:

1. Allow other apps to run commands:
 echo "allow-external-apps=true" >> ~/.termux/termux.properties
 termux-reload-settings

2. Create the virtual environment (if you have not yet):
 python -m venv ~/myproject/.venv

Then grant pynb the "Run commands in Termux environment" permission when asked.

Tip: for numpy / matplotlib, run "pkg install python-numpy matplotlib" and create the venv with --system-site-packages.
Termux is not installed. Install Termux from F-Droid or GitHub to run cells on this phone, or use an SSH server.
Without the \"Run commands in Termux environment\" permission pynb cannot start Python in Termux. You can grant it in Android settings → Apps → pynb → Permissions.

Runs cells on a Linux or macOS server (AWS EC2, a VPS, a home server…) over SSH.

On the server, once:
 python3 -m venv ~/myproject/.venv
 ~/myproject/.venv/bin/pip install numpy pandas matplotlib

EC2: the user is usually ec2-user (Amazon Linux), ubuntu (Ubuntu) or admin (Debian), and the key is your .pem file. The security group only needs inbound SSH (port 22); the kernel listens on the server's localhost and is reached through the SSH tunnel.

Code, files, %pip and !shell commands run on the server. The notebook is still saved on this phone. Keys and passwords are stored encrypted with the Android Keystore.
